# Message matrix: spec versus implementations

Every message of [`wsh-v1.yaml`](wsh-v1.yaml) and whether each implementation **names** it: sends it or acts on it in code that is
neither generated nor a test. `yes` means a handler or a sender exists; `-` means nothing in that implementation has heard of the message
(the Rust types still decode it, since every message is generated into both languages; the JS decoder passes it through).
It does not say that every field is honoured: [`test/spec-conformance.test.mjs`](../test/spec-conformance.test.mjs) and the interop tests do that.
How it is derived, and which files count for which column, is in the header of [`scripts/message-matrix.mjs`](../scripts/message-matrix.mjs).
A column is the whole implementation of that role: **JS host** = `createWshServer`, `createMemoryHost`, `createReverseHost`, the relay;
**JS client** = `WshClient` and its helpers; **Rust host** = `wsh-server`; **Rust client** = `wsh-client` and the `wsh` CLI.
Which messages a peer may RECEIVE without negotiating, and what to do about a message a peer does not know, is in [COMPATIBILITY.md](../COMPATIBILITY.md).
